books.title: The Pinnacle of Reality
books.description: An Epic Tale of Reality and Destiny

pages.content:
The Realist sped across the street, narrowly avoiding an Itineror which swerved and broadsided into a streetlight. He vaulted over the rail protecting pedestrians from the roads and ducked behind a parked Itineror beside a transport parts shop.

The Itineror was an old model, and the large gas exhaust protruded crookedly from the underside. He crouched underneath this, trying to make himself as small as possible and blend into the drab grey color of the vehicle, matching his clothes. He breathed deeply, tired from the short chase. He was not old, but flashes of pain ran down the length of his body. So many scars…

Suddenly, the ground beneath him began to tremble. At that very moment, his head began to ache. This ache turned into a sharp pain that filled his mind, seeming to gnaw at his thoughts, scattering them. He must leave now, or he would weaken too much. But if he was exposed, out in the open, it would find him. The pain moved to wrap against his skull, and he groaned softly. With the consciousness that was left to him, he decided to leave the cover of the Itineror for somewhere else - anywhere where the unbearable waves boring into his head weren’t. He’d be quickly incapacitated otherwise.

He scrambled out from behind the Itineror on all fours, his thoughts all bent on how best to escape. But he couldn’t think, with energy draining out of him as the seconds passed. Then his gaze rested on the Itineror, and an idea sparked in his dulling mind.

He picked up a long metal pole lying beside him - the result of the Itineror which he’d barely avoided - and stabbed it into the narrow space between the door of the Itineror and its metal plating, hoping to use it as a lever to open the door. But his strength was fading fast, and his already weak attempts slackened. He ducked back behind the Itineror again. There had to be another way to do this, one that wouldn’t reveal himself.

But as he strained to concentrate, the air was filled with a sound. The sound of pistons, gears, and other mechanical parts, clicking to an unknown rhythm. It was coming closer, and with that realization, a strange calmness overcame him. He had no choice now, so there was no point in worrying.

pages.content:
The mother was not surprised when something exploded two feet away from her, overwhelming her vision with the red and orange of fire, and she was thrown into an out-of-control spiral.

The wind screamed past her, the ground approaching, harsh and stern, her erratically flapping wings weak, grey and red blurring through her eyes. More wing flapping eventually allowed her to regain her balance, talons hitting the ground solidly, pain zinging up into her legs.

There were innumerable craters defacing the ground scattered around her, all a terrible witness to the death and destruction occurring. Each was filled with blood, death, decay: it was too much to bear thinking about. But she had to, for the sake of her egg, because her egg could be in any one of these.

And yet… it could be anywhere, even crushed under a dead dragon. But, in her heart, the life of the egg pulsed, tied to her. It had to be alive.

She tired and landed again, but once she had regained her strength she spread her wings and took off, flying low. She swept the ground with her eyes, scanning every grain for some sign of her egg.

As she headed closer and closer to the battle, the number of stray arrows and explosives increased. She hoped she could find her egg before — no, she couldn't, wouldn't think about that — wait. Why would the humans use arrows if they had explosives? Her thoughts were cut short when a volley of weaponry blasted towards her, arrows and debris flaming orange. She somersaulted and spun in response, letting herself be lost in the dance of the wind, just the once.

She landed - she needed to keep closer to the ground. The air was too exposed. A hiss. A rip. Then red hot blades slicing into her wing.

An arrow. The thought drifted across the haze of pain blanketing her mind, her vision filled with the black shaft. She took a breath, allowing the breeze to clear her head, steeling herself. She gripped the arrow in her teeth and wrenched it out. Her vision went red. She slumped, gasping, as the shaft clattered to the stones.

A fleeting glimpse of black blazing past. Then a heavy thud, thick and wet. She glimpsed scales behind her - but the dragon would be fine. An arrow alone could not kill a dragon. Then the arrow exploded.

Instantly the dragon was gone, vaporized.

She thought of the arrow which had hit her; if she hadn't removed it, she would be dead. Even as she looked back, the arrow detonated, creating another crater.

She began moving again, everything around her a mesh of dull grey, her wing dragging, scraping on the stones, just... moving.

She stumbled. The ground gave way beneath her - a flash of the sky - red, rushing towards her - a splash - and she was still. A cold liquid - blood, she realized, sloshed against her scales and her eyes cleared, taking in the grey walls of the crater around her. She brought her talons under her, pushing against the soft, murky ground, ignoring the searing stabs around her wing. She turned in a full circle, noting the steep, jagged walls, and realized she couldn't get out till she could fly.

Then, in the very center of the crater, she saw her egg. Her heart lifted, biting agony soothed, an energy thrumming through her as she reached for it, not noticing the arrow which slid into the water with barely a ripple, inches from her egg.

Then, the world exploded.

Commander-in-chief of the Royal Empire of the Fittus was fuming.

"Why were you worthless guards altering the formation? I clearly mentioned that you were not to change your formation, not even in the most dire of situations till I give the command!"

"But-"

The guard was not allowed to finish, because the commander-in-chief struck his chest. He did this with such force that the guard flew several feet before he fell to the ground, unconscious.

"Now," said the commander, "remove your unworthy selves from my presence. All of you." He spat on the ground and spread his wings, flying back to the underground cave system that was the home of all Fittus members.

But an irritatingly noble voice in his mind stopped him. At least you have a home, it said. Exploded suppressed a grunt — this voice was... right. He should be grateful. But his feelings still chafed underneath his scales.

He began to pace again. The commander was probably dealing with guards — perhaps, just this once, he would forget to call on Exploded. But he shook this thought off; he refused to give himself false hopes.

As he moved across the cave, the walls seemed to push in closer. He lifted his wings instead, taking off, denying the walls. Wind rushed at him, but he cleanly cut through, circling his cave. No matter what the commander planned for him - whatever happened - he would still have the freedom of flight. He would still lift his wings, deny the world, take to the sky.

The sky.

It was now that he wanted more than to be outside. Yet the commander only called on him after the time that Fittus members were allowed to fly free. True enough, guards monitored them at all sides - any attempt to escape would be severely punished - but still. The clear blues filled his mind, the thrill of speed, the calm greens of forest below. But the dark grey of the walls stood starkly against the blue - refusing to give freedom.

A small ache pulsed in the base of his wings - brought on by the demanding angle that his wings were forced at to fly in a sharp circle - and so he slowed, descending, at last alighting again on the stone floor.

From the passageway just outside the entrance to his cave, he heard the echoing clacks of talons that announced the coming of another dragon. A messenger, he decided, with a sinking of heart, that came to summon him to the commander’s cave. He slumped, wings falling slackly around his body. Despite all his efforts, he had hoped - and like always, he was disappointed.

He turned towards the entrance as a dark yellow dragon with splashes of black scales appeared.

“The commander summons you to his cave.”

Then the messenger was gone, turning curtly and disappearing down another passage. Suppressing a groan, Exploded exited his cave, turning into the familiar path - too familiar, even. He’d walked its length every day since he could remember.

Exploded stood hesitantly in front of the entrance to the commander’s cave. He knew he shouldn’t dawdle, but…

Enough. He should be braver than this. He stepped in.

Immediately, he straightened and assumed the position every Fittus member was taught when in the presence of the commander — wings tucked, head bowed, and every muscle locked into place. The commander's presence seemed to weigh on him, a cold pressure which made his scales prickle.

The commander's steps echoed as he circled slowly, each movement deliberate and predatory.

"Well, well," said the commander.

"I have summoned you here for an arrangement of power," he said, voice smooth, polished. "For countless years, the Fittus was governed under the same hierarchy — strength above all, lineage above strength, and tradition above both."

He paused behind Exploded, so close that the younger dragon felt the faint heat of his breath, sending shivers down his spine.

"Yet... following the ways of our forefathers is often the path to destruction. We must blaze a new path should we aim for true strength.

"Tradition rewards the loudest roars, not the sharpest minds. It crowns the largest wings, not the most capable claws."

Exploded swallowed. He was unsure how to act — should he agree or remain silent? But the commander gave him no time to decide.

He stepped into view again, wings half-spread. Not a gesture of threat, Exploded thought, but it wasn't comforting either. Something about the posture implied absolute dominance and control.

"I have watched brilliance buried beneath nobility; potential wasted because law demanded it."

The commander's tone changed slightly. Still cool and calm, but an added hint touched his voice, and his eyes narrowed slightly, black and depthless. His next words were spoken with a strange finality to them.

"I will not allow the Fittus to crack under the weight of its own arrogance."

Exploded's heart hammered. What did the commander want from him?

"From this day forward," the commander continued, "rank will be earned through trials — real deeds. Hunts, missions, and trials that reveal who a dragon is, not who tradition claims they should be."

The commander began to pace again, tail sweeping the stone floor with a soft scrape. "Dragons of cunning will face cunning. A dragon of strength will face claws and wings to rival them. Each dragon will face what they excel at."

Exploded found himself agreeing with the commander; he, too, did not find the hierarchy fair. So he dared a glance upward. The commander's expression was still neutral; neither cruel, nor kind, but calculating.

"These tests will not be announced," the commander said. "They will not be explained, nor questioned."

"The others will believe the trials are natural. Let them. Ambition grows best when it believes it is unseen."

Exploded made to speak, then stopped himself. Why was the commander telling him this, anyway? How was he special or different?

The commander's gaze suddenly fixed on Exploded, pinning him to where he stood. You wonder why I tell you this," the commander murmured. "It is because new blood adapts fastest. You are young. Unshaped. And… Hungry."

Exploded's breath caught. He had never been addressed so directly - and he had never spoken the question aloud. A cold chill set in, and he felt his scales shifting, clicking together quietly. Something was missing.

The commander stepped closer, staring at Exploded directly in the eye. Exploded wanted to look away, but the commander's eyes pulled him into their fathomless depths.

"If you are worthy, you will rise. You will fall if you are not. And only you will know that the trials are chosen — not random. Carry this knowledge carefully. Power is sharp - when mishandled, it cuts.”

The commander dismissed Exploded with a flick of his tail.

"You may leave."

A thrilling hum rushed through him as he turned, the caves around him melting together as he rushed through them. But his thoughts scattered and gusted before he could catch them, cool relief fighting with agitation bubbling up inside of him.

Words flitted through his mind — who was he, anyway? Why did the commander need him, in the first place?

But he couldn't organize and follow the thoughts. They rushed around him in waves. Had the commander really spoke to him? Addressed him directly? Revealed... secrets? He felt the taunting tinge of the last piece. Something that would fix it all.

Did he want strength? Did he really want position? Did the commander want... equality? The conclusion grew stronger. He forced himself to concentrate. But an energy thrummed through his mind, shattering his focus.

Lying. The commander was lying. No — Exploded was lying. To himself. A dream? Trust — he couldn't trust himself. Or the commander. Or... anything. Nothing was real.
